Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Pawan Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the complainant and learned AGA for the State as well as perused the record.

The instant application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 714 of 2023, under Sections 419,
420, 467, 468, 471, 427, 323, 504 and 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Akbarpur,
District Ambedkar Nagar.
Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is noway involved in committing the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the instant matter.
He submits that there was a dispute in between the parties with respect to Committee of Management and due to animosity, the story is cooked up and applicant is implicated.
Further submission is that the applicant has cooperated in the investigation proceeding and the chargesheet has been filed and now no custodial interrogation is required.

He also added that the applicant is a law abiding citizen and there is no criminal antecedent of the applicant and he undertakes that he would always remain present over there on his requirement, thus, submission is that the applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the complainant has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that conduct of the applicant is against the law and he has committed cheat and fraud, as he fabricated certain documents with respect to Committee of Management and regarding appointment of certain teachers and, therefore, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: List/put up this matter in the second week of March, 2025.
In the meantime, learned counsel for the opposite parties may file their counter affidavits."

From perusal of the order dated 12.2.2025, it transpires that learned State Counsel as well as the counsel for the complainant were directed to file counter affidavit but the same has not been filed as yet.
Learned State Counsel has failed to demonstrate that there is any adversarial fact which are pleaded in the bail application.
This Court finds that the applicant was enlarged on an interim anticipatory bail after thoroughly considering the merits of the case.

The learned counsel for the State has also failed to submit any fact that the applicant is not cooperating with the investigation proceedings or otherwise any glaring fact which can adversely affect the merit of the case.
